gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: If the walls ___ soundproofed, we would not hear the neighbours.
gaps.hint: unreal present with the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: If the museum opened on Mondays, we ___ visit tomorrow.
gaps.hint: unreal condition with a possible result
gaps.explanation: An unreal condition takes 'could' in the result to show what would then be possible: could.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ your shoes in the middle of the floor!
gaps.hint: irritation about a habit, wish would
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'would' expresses irritation about a habit you want changed: would not leave.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.
